```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Scholl et al. (2018) gave 84 healthy volunteers capsules of a green tea
extract standardised to 150 mg epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) twice daily
for four days and one capsule on the morning of day 5, then sampled plasma
for 9 h. They fitted three **independently developed** two-compartment
population PK models, one per catechin measured in plasma. The library
therefore ships three model files that share this vignette:

| Model | Catechin | Dose per capsule | Absorption |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Scholl_2018_egcg` | epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) | 150 mg | zero-order dissolution (D1) into depot, lagged first-order ka |
| `Scholl_2018_egc` | epigallocatechin (EGC) | 18 mg | lagged first-order ka |
| `Scholl_2018_ecg` | epicatechin gallate (ECG) | 35 mg | zero-order dissolution (D1) into depot, lagged first-order ka |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Scholl_2018_egcg"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0193074> (open access)
* Modeling Supplement (S6 File, the three NONMEM control streams):
  <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0193074.s006>
* Concentration data (S1 File): <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0193074.s001>

```{r models}
mod_egcg <- readModelDb("Scholl_2018_egcg")
mod_egc <- readModelDb("Scholl_2018_egc")
mod_ecg <- readModelDb("Scholl_2018_ecg")
```

# Population

`r rxode2::rxode(mod_egcg)$population$notes` Participants were 19-49 years old
(mean 24.5), weighed 68.0 kg on average (SD 11.7) and had a BMI of 18-30
kg/m^2 (Table 1). All were of Western European ancestry and free of acute or
chronic disease; 54 were women, of whom 37 used oral contraceptives. The
capsules were taken with a meal on days 1-4 and after an overnight fast on day
5. Sampling on day 5 was pre-dose and at 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 9 h.

Gender, age, weight, height, BMI, smoking, alcohol, habitual tea drinking and
blood counts were screened and not retained. The retained covariates are
genotypes of drug transporters and phase II enzymes (accepted at the
exploratory threshold p <= 0.025) and, for EGC, oral-contraceptive use.

# Source trace

All structural values are the final estimates in Scholl 2018 Table 3; the
model structure and the covariate parameterisations are those of the S6 File
control streams (`$PK`, `$DES`, `$ERROR`).

| Element | EGCG | EGC | ECG | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ka (1/h) | 1.86 | 0.830 | 1.78 | Table 3; S6 `K12 = THETA(1)` |
| CL/F (L/h) | 148 | 560 | 196 | Table 3 |
| Vcentral/F (L) | 334 | 1180 | 395 | Table 3 |
| Q/F (L/h) | 59.7 | 324 | 56.2 | Table 3 |
| Vperipheral/F (L) | 1260 | 10100 | 1300 | Table 3 |
| D1 (h) | 0.301 | -- | 0.422 | Table 3; S6 `D1`, `RATE` in `$INPUT` |
| Lag time (h) | 0.327 | 0.413 | 0.319 | Table 3; S6 `ALAG` |
| F | 1 (fixed) | 1 (fixed) | 1 (fixed) | Table 3; S6 `$THETA (1 FIX)` |
| IIV ka / CL / D1 / F / lag (%CV) | 79 / 25 / 103 / 46 / 32 | -- / 38 / -- / 37 / 11 | 78 / 39 / 70 / 57 / 43 | Table 3 |
| IIV Vcentral/F / Q/F (%CV) | -- | 80 / 92 | -- | Table 3 |
| Proportional / additive residual | 17 % / 5 ug/L | 28 % / -- | 18 % / 1 ug/L | Table 3; S6 `Y = IPRED*(1+EPS(1))+EPS(2)` |
| SLCO1B1 rs4149056 on CL/F | `*(1 - 0.152 x C-allele count)` | -- | -- | Table 3; S6 `CL = THETA(2)*(1+OATP41EFF*OATP41T)`; Table 5 |
| ABCC2 rs717620 on F | `* 0.740` if C/C | -- | -- | Table 3; S6 `IF (MRP71T.EQ.0)`; Table 5 |
| Contraceptives on Vcentral/F | -- | `* 0.450` | -- | Table 3 `CONCEP`; S6; Table 5 |
| ABCC2 rs717620 on Vcentral/F | -- | `*(1 - 0.370 x T-allele count)` | -- | Table 3; S6 `(1+MRP71EFF*MRP71T)`; Table 5 |
| ABCC2 rs3740066 on Q/F | -- | `* 2.33` if C/C | -- | Table 3; S6 `IF (MRP37T.EQ.0)`; Table 5 |
| SLCO1B1 rs2306283 on CL/F | -- | `* 0.653` if A/A | -- | Table 3; S6 `IF (OATP23T.EQ.0)`; Table 5 |
| UGT1A1*28 on CL/F | -- | `* 0.744` if (TA)6/(TA)6 | -- | Table 3; S6 `IF (UGT.EQ.0)`; Table 5 |
| COMT rs4680 on F | -- | `* 0.760` if A/A | -- | Table 3; S6 `IF (COMT.EQ.2)`; Table 5 |
| ODEs (depot -> central <-> peripheral, CL from central) | all | all | all | S6 `$DES` |
| Concentration = amount / Vcentral x 1000 (mg, L -> ug/L) | all | all | all | S6 `S2 = V2/1000` |

## Scale of the IIV column

Table 3 prints IIV as %CV without a conversion formula, and the Methods state
that omega "expresses approximately the coefficient of variation". The ECG
control stream in the S6 File carries an `$OMEGA BLOCK(5)` whose initial
estimates were evidently seeded from a near-final run. Pushing each initial
variance through both candidate readings shows which one the table uses:

```{r omega-scale}
omega_init <- c(ka = 0.571, CL = 0.137, D1 = 0.619, F = 0.32, lag = 0.186) # S6 File ECG $OMEGA BLOCK(5) diagonal
cv_table <- c(ka = 78, CL = 39, D1 = 70, F = 57, lag = 43) # Table 3 ECG IIV %CV
omega_chk <- data.frame(
  parameter = names(omega_init),
  table_cv = cv_table,
  sqrt_omega = round(100 * sqrt(omega_init), 1),
  lognormal_cv = round(100 * sqrt(exp(omega_init) - 1), 1)
)
knitr::kable(
  omega_chk |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Parameter" = parameter,
      "Table 3 %CV" = table_cv,
      "100 x omega" = sqrt_omega,
      "Log-normal CV%" = lognormal_cv
    ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
err_sqrt <- abs(omega_chk$sqrt_omega - omega_chk$table_cv)
err_logn <- abs(omega_chk$lognormal_cv - omega_chk$table_cv)
stopifnot(
  # F and lag time sit exactly on 100 x omega and 2-5 points off the
  # log-normal reading; the largest variances (ka, D1) discriminate hardest.
  sum(err_sqrt < err_logn) >= 4,
  all(err_sqrt[omega_chk$parameter %in% c("F", "lag")] < 0.5)
)
```

The `100 x omega` reading tracks the table for four of the five entries and
reproduces F and lag time exactly, so all three models encode
`omega^2 = (CV/100)^2`.

# Virtual cohort

Genotypes are drawn independently from the observed genotype counts (Table 4)
and contraceptive use from the observed 37 of 84 participants. Each catechin
model uses only the covariates it needs. 200 subjects are simulated per
catechin.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2018)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2018)
n_sub <- 200
draw_geno <- function(n, counts) sample(0:2, n, replace = TRUE, prob = counts)
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  mrp71t = draw_geno(n_sub, c(58, 22, 3)), # ABCC2 rs717620 CC/CT/TT
  oatp41t = draw_geno(n_sub, c(54, 27, 3)), # SLCO1B1 rs4149056 TT/CT/CC
  oatp23t = draw_geno(n_sub, c(29, 40, 15)), # SLCO1B1 rs2306283 AA/GA/GG
  mrp37t = draw_geno(n_sub, c(40, 32, 12)), # ABCC2 rs3740066 CC/CT/TT
  ugt = draw_geno(n_sub, c(37, 37, 10)), # UGT1A1*28 (-)/(-/TA)/TA
  comt = draw_geno(n_sub, c(14, 47, 23)), # COMT rs4680 GG/GA/AA
  CONMED_BIRTHCONTROL = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 37 / 84)
) |>
  mutate(
    SNP_ABCC2_RS717620_HET = as.integer(mrp71t == 1),
    SNP_ABCC2_RS717620_HOM = as.integer(mrp71t == 2),
    SNP_SLCO1B1_RS4149056_HET = as.integer(oatp41t == 1),
    SNP_SLCO1B1_RS4149056_HOM = as.integer(oatp41t == 2),
    SNP_SLCO1B1_RS2306283_HET = as.integer(oatp23t == 1),
    SNP_SLCO1B1_RS2306283_HOM = as.integer(oatp23t == 2),
    SNP_ABCC2_RS3740066_HET = as.integer(mrp37t == 1),
    SNP_ABCC2_RS3740066_HOM = as.integer(mrp37t == 2),
    SNP_UGT1A1_RS8175347_HET = as.integer(ugt == 1),
    SNP_UGT1A1_RS8175347_HOM = as.integer(ugt == 2),
    SNP_COMT_RS4680_HOM = as.integer(comt == 2)
  )
```

# Simulation of the study

Doses are given at 0, 12, ..., 96 h (eight doses on days 1-4 and the day-5
morning dose). EGCG and ECG doses carry `rate = -2` so that the modelled
dissolution duration D1 applies; EGC doses are boluses into the depot.

```{r events}
catechins <- data.frame(
  analyte = c("EGCG", "EGC", "ECG"),
  dose = c(150, 18, 35),
  rate = c(-2, 0, -2)
)
model_of <- list(EGCG = mod_egcg, EGC = mod_egc, ECG = mod_ecg)

make_events <- function(dose, rate, dose_times, obs_times, cov_df) {
  doses <- expand.grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), time = dose_times)
  doses$amt <- dose
  doses$evid <- 1L
  doses$rate <- rate
  obs <- expand.grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), time = obs_times)
  obs$amt <- 0
  obs$evid <- 0L
  obs$rate <- 0
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(cmt = "depot") |>
    mutate(cmt = ifelse(evid == 0L, "central", cmt)) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    left_join(cov_df, by = "id")
}

# cov_df is one covariate frame for all catechins, or a list of frames
# named by catechin.
simulate_catechin <- function(i, dose_times, obs_times, cov_df) {
  if (!is.data.frame(cov_df)) cov_df <- cov_df[[catechins$analyte[i]]]
  ev <- make_events(catechins$dose[i], catechins$rate[i], dose_times, obs_times, cov_df)
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(model_of[[catechins$analyte[i]]], ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  sim$analyte <- catechins$analyte[i]
  sim
}

study_times <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9)
day5 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(catechins)), simulate_catechin,
  dose_times = 12 * (0:8), obs_times = 96 + seq(0, 12, by = 0.25),
  cov_df = cohort
)) |>
  mutate(tad = time - 96)
```

## Visual predictive check (Figure 6)

The S1 File publishes every measured concentration. The observed 5th, 50th
and 95th percentiles per sampling time below were computed by the maintainers
from that file (values below the limit of detection are missing there; the
`n` column shows how many were quantified, which falls to 27 of 84 for EGC
before the dose and 34 of 84 at 9 h).

```{r observed}
observed <- data.frame(
  analyte = rep(c("EGCG", "EGC", "ECG"), each = 9),
  tad = rep(study_times, 3),
  n = c(
    82, 80, 82, 81, 80, 81, 80, 80, 77,
    27, 71, 81, 81, 77, 76, 71, 62, 34,
    69, 79, 82, 81, 80, 81, 79, 77, 67
  ),
  p05 = c(
    5.55, 16.2, 57.1, 92.5, 58, 37.6, 24.3, 13, 8.29,
    0.794, 1.09, 2.46, 2.21, 1.78, 1.34, 1.02, 0.411, 0.658,
    -0.501, 0.774, 9.29, 17.1, 10.1, 6.84, 3.76, 0.0764, -0.704
  ),
  p50 = c(
    23.5, 50.6, 159, 179, 138, 96.3, 64.5, 33.4, 23.6,
    2.57, 3.09, 6.78, 6.43, 4.99, 3.59, 2.69, 2.05, 1.47,
    3.27, 8.51, 34.5, 40, 28.5, 21, 13, 5.44, 3.53
  ),
  p95 = c(
    58.6, 238, 573, 408, 283, 188, 136, 70.6, 47.6,
    10.6, 14.7, 22.5, 16.5, 10.7, 7.87, 6.84, 7.55, 8.27,
    13.3, 44.6, 111, 97.2, 63.4, 44.2, 30.3, 15.5, 10.2
  )
)

vpc <- day5 |>
  filter(tad <= 9) |>
  group_by(analyte, tad) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(sim, 0.05), med = median(sim), hi = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
vpc$analyte <- factor(vpc$analyte, levels = catechins$analyte)
observed$analyte <- factor(observed$analyte, levels = catechins$analyte)

ggplot(vpc, aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(y = med)) +
  geom_point(data = observed, aes(y = p50), colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_point(data = observed, aes(y = p95), colour = "firebrick", shape = 2) +
  geom_point(data = observed, aes(y = p05), colour = "firebrick", shape = 6) +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the day-5 dose (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (ug/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Line and band: simulated median and 90% prediction interval.",
      "Points: observed median and 5th/95th percentiles (S1 File)."
    )
  )
```

Replicates Figure 6 of Scholl 2018 (linear panels). The simulated median is
compared with the observed median at every sampling time after the dose:

```{r vpc-check}
vpc_chk <- observed |>
  filter(tad > 0) |>
  inner_join(vpc, by = c("analyte", "tad")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (med - p50) / p50)
knitr::kable(
  vpc_chk |>
    select(analyte, tad, p50, med, pct_diff) |>
    mutate(med = signif(med, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Catechin" = analyte,
      "Time after dose (h)" = tad,
      "Observed median (ug/L)" = p50,
      "Simulated median (ug/L)" = med,
      "% difference" = pct_diff
    ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
vpc_summary <- vpc_chk |>
  group_by(analyte) |>
  summarise(median_abs_pct = median(abs(pct_diff)), .groups = "drop")
vpc_summary
stopifnot(
  # A dose, unit (mg -> ug/L) or clearance error moves every time point by a
  # factor of two or more; residual differences of up to about 20 % come from the
  # 200-subject draw and from below-LoD values missing from the observed side.
  all(vpc_summary$median_abs_pct < 30)
)
```

## Steady-state identity (deterministic)

At steady state the AUC over one dosing interval must equal `F x Dose / CL`
for every individual. The typical ECG subject (no covariates) is dosed for 20
days and integrated over the last interval on a fine grid:

```{r ss-identity}
ss_ev <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = 12 * (0:39), amt = 35, evid = 1L, rate = -2, cmt = "depot"
) |>
  bind_rows(data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = 468 + seq(0, 12, by = 0.01), amt = 0, evid = 0L, rate = 0,
    cmt = "central"
  )) |>
  arrange(time, desc(evid))
ss_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ecg), ss_ev, returnType = "data.frame")
auc_tau <- with(ss_sim, sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2))
auc_expected <- 35 / 196 * 1000
c(auc_tau = auc_tau, expected = auc_expected)
stopifnot(abs(auc_tau / auc_expected - 1) < 0.01)
```

# Single-dose and steady-state exposure (Figure 8)

Scholl 2018 simulated 1000 subjects per catechin after a single dose and at
steady state (12-hourly dosing) and reported median AUC0-12 values in the
Results text, without saying which covariate values the simulation used.
The same is done here for the virtual cohort above (study covariate mix) and,
separately, with every covariate effect switched off: each subject is given
the genotype for which all covariate multipliers equal 1, so only the Table 3
typical values and IIV remain. Because the reference stratum of ABCC2
rs717620 differs between the EGCG model (T carriers) and the EGC model (C/C),
this second cohort is built per catechin.

```{r fig8}
no_cov <- cohort |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("SNP_"), ~0L), CONMED_BIRTHCONTROL = 0L)
cohort_off <- list(
  # F multiplier 1 for ABCC2 rs717620 T carriers; CL multiplier 1 for rs4149056 T/T.
  EGCG = no_cov |> mutate(SNP_ABCC2_RS717620_HET = 1L),
  # Multipliers 1 for rs717620 C/C, rs3740066 and rs2306283 variant carriers,
  # UGT1A1*28 carriers, COMT G carriers and no contraceptive use.
  EGC = no_cov |> mutate(
    SNP_ABCC2_RS3740066_HET = 1L, SNP_SLCO1B1_RS2306283_HET = 1L,
    SNP_UGT1A1_RS8175347_HET = 1L
  ),
  ECG = no_cov
)

auc012 <- function(sim, start) {
  sim |>
    filter(time >= start, time <= start + 12) |>
    group_by(analyte, id) |>
    summarise(
      auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

run_fig8 <- function(cov_df, label) {
  sd_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(catechins)), simulate_catechin,
    dose_times = 0, obs_times = seq(0, 12, by = 0.05), cov_df = cov_df
  ))
  ss_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(catechins)), simulate_catechin,
    dose_times = 12 * (0:19), obs_times = 228 + seq(0, 12, by = 0.05), cov_df = cov_df
  ))
  bind_rows(
    auc012(sd_sim, 0) |> mutate(regimen = "Single dose"),
    auc012(ss_sim, 228) |> mutate(regimen = "Steady state")
  ) |>
    group_by(analyte, regimen) |>
    summarise(median_auc = median(auc), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(cohort = label)
}
```

```{r fig8-run}
fig8 <- bind_rows(
  run_fig8(cohort, "Study genotype mix"),
  run_fig8(cohort_off, "Covariate effects off")
)
published_fig8 <- data.frame(
  analyte = rep(c("EGCG", "EGC", "ECG"), each = 2),
  regimen = rep(c("Single dose", "Steady state"), 3),
  published = c(657.0, 902.0, 15.8, 30.4, 144.2, 176.7)
)
fig8_tbl <- fig8 |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = cohort, values_from = median_auc) |>
  left_join(published_fig8, by = c("analyte", "regimen")) |>
  mutate(
    pct_mix = round(100 * (`Study genotype mix` - published) / published, 1),
    pct_off = round(100 * (`Covariate effects off` - published) / published, 1),
    `Study genotype mix` = round(`Study genotype mix`, 1),
    `Covariate effects off` = round(`Covariate effects off`, 1)
  )
fig8_tbl$analyte <- factor(fig8_tbl$analyte, levels = catechins$analyte)
fig8_tbl <- arrange(fig8_tbl, analyte, regimen)
knitr::kable(
  fig8_tbl |>
    select(analyte, regimen, published, `Study genotype mix`, pct_mix, `Covariate effects off`, pct_off) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Catechin" = analyte,
      "Regimen" = regimen,
      "Published median AUC0-12 (h*ug/L)" = published,
      "Simulated, study mix" = `Study genotype mix`,
      "% diff (study mix)" = pct_mix,
      "Simulated, covariate effects off" = `Covariate effects off`,
      "% diff (effects off)" = pct_off
    ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
accumulation <- fig8 |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = regimen, values_from = median_auc) |>
  mutate(ratio = round(`Steady state` / `Single dose`, 2)) |>
  select(analyte, cohort, ratio) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = cohort, values_from = ratio) |>
  left_join(
    published_fig8 |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = regimen, values_from = published) |>
      mutate(Published = round(`Steady state` / `Single dose`, 2)) |>
      select(analyte, Published),
    by = "analyte"
  )
accumulation
gallates <- filter(fig8_tbl, analyte %in% c("EGCG", "ECG"))
stopifnot(
  # EGCG and ECG: the study genotype mix reproduces all four published medians.
  all(abs(gallates$pct_mix) < 15)
)
```

EGCG and ECG reproduce the published single-dose and steady-state medians
with the study covariate mix. For EGC the study mix reproduces the published
accumulation ratio (steady state over single dose, about 1.9), but both
medians sit about a quarter above the published 15.8 and 30.4 h*ug/L, a level
shift in `F / CL`. Switching the covariate effects off brings the EGC
steady-state median close to the published value but not the single-dose one,
and lowers the accumulation ratio, because the ABCC2 rs3740066 effect on Q/F
then disappears. The covariate set-up of the published simulation is not
reported, so this gap cannot be attributed further. The day-5 VPC above and
the NCA comparison below show that the EGC model with the study genotype mix
reproduces the **observed** concentrations and the observed AUC0-9.

# Non-compartmental analysis on day 5 (Table 2)

PKNCA is run on the simulated day-5 profiles at the study sampling times
(0-9 h after the dose), as Scholl 2018 did with Phoenix WinNonlin (linear
trapezoidal rule, AUC to the last sample). Two choices make the simulated
values comparable with Table 2:

* The concentrations include residual error (`sim`), because the observed NCA
  was run on measured data and the maximum of noisy samples is biased upward
  relative to the noise-free prediction. Negative simulated values (additive
  error near zero) are set to 0.
* The Table 2 central values are **means**: the mean tmax of 1.6 h for EGCG
  and 1.7 h for ECG cannot be a median of the sampling times 1 and 2 h. The
  simulated individual NCA values are therefore averaged with the mean as
  well.

```{r nca}
nca_conc <- day5 |>
  filter(tad %in% study_times, !is.na(sim)) |>
  mutate(treatment = analyte, conc = pmax(sim, 0)) |>
  select(id, tad, conc, treatment)
nca_dose <- catechins |>
  rename(treatment = analyte) |>
  tidyr::crossing(id = seq_len(n_sub)) |>
  mutate(tad = 0) |>
  select(id, tad, dose, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, conc ~ tad | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, dose ~ tad | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 9,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

reference_nca <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("EGCG", "EGC", "ECG"),
  cmax = c(275.4, 10.7, 60.1),
  tmax = c(1.6, 1.5, 1.7),
  auclast = c(877.9, 35.1, 183.6),
  half.life = c(2.6, 3.9, 1.8)
)
nca_mean <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
nca_tbl <- ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_mean, reference_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/L", tmax = "h", auclast = "h*ug/L", half.life = "h")
)
knitr::kable(nca_tbl, row.names = FALSE)
```

`r attr(nca_tbl, "footnote")`

```{r nca-check}
nca_wide <- nca_mean |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  inner_join(reference_nca, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_sim", "_ref"))
stopifnot(
  # AUC0-9 integrates F x Dose / CL over the interval; a dose, unit or
  # clearance error shows up here first.
  all(abs(nca_wide$auclast_sim / nca_wide$auclast_ref - 1) < 0.15),
  all(abs(nca_wide$cmax_sim / nca_wide$cmax_ref - 1) < 0.25)
)
```

The reference values are the means of Scholl 2018 Table 2 (observed NCA on
day 5, 84 subjects). AUC0-9, Cmax and tmax agree with the observed values for
all three catechins. The terminal half-life is overestimated by the simulated
NCA, most for EGC: over a 9 h window the log-linear fit mixes the
distribution and the slow terminal phase of a two-compartment profile (EGC
peripheral volume 10,100 L), a mean of individual half-lives is pulled up by
a few flat noisy tails, and the observed EGC half-life rests on few
quantifiable late samples (34 of 84 at 9 h).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Three independent models.** Scholl 2018 fitted EGCG, EGC and ECG as three
  separate NONMEM problems on the same subjects (`IGNORE(ANALYTE.NE.n)` in each
  S6 File stream); they are packaged as three model files. No between-catechin
  correlation is modelled, although the paper reports strongly correlated AUCs
  (Figure 4).
* **IIV scale.** Table 3 %CV values are encoded as `omega^2 = (CV/100)^2`; the
  evidence is the ECG `$OMEGA` initial-estimate check above and the paper's
  own statement that omega approximates the CV.
* **ECG IIV correlations.** The S6 File ECG stream estimates a full
  `$OMEGA BLOCK(5)`, but Table 3 reports only the variances. The unreported
  covariances are set to zero; the block's initial estimates are not final
  values and are not used. Individual-level ECG simulations therefore lose
  the correlation between, for example, ka and D1.
* **Residual error.** The Table 3 proportional (%) and additive (ug/L) values
  are read as standard deviations; the S6 File `$ERROR` blocks are
  `Y = IPRED*(1+EPS(1)) + EPS(2)` (EGCG, ECG) and `Y = IPRED*(1+EPS(1))` (EGC),
  encoded as `prop() + add()` and `prop()`.
* **Dose per catechin.** Each model is dosed with the mg of its own catechin
  per capsule (150 mg EGCG, 18 mg EGC, 35 mg ECG; Study drug section). The
  S6 File scales concentration by `S2 = V2/1000` (mg and L to ug/L), and
  dose / AUC reproduces the Table 2 CL/F of each catechin, which confirms the
  per-catechin dose. The capsule content is stated as approximate.
* **Food.** Doses on days 1-4 were taken with a meal and the day-5 dose after
  an overnight fast; the models have no food effect, as in the source.
* **Lag times.** The text quotes 19 min (EGCG, ECG) and 25 min (EGC), which
  match the Table 3 values of 0.32-0.33 h and 0.413 h.
* **Central volume in the Discussion.** The Discussion quotes a central volume
  of 425 L for EGCG; Table 3 and the fitted model give 334 L, which is used.
* **Missing genotype.** One participant had no ABCC2 rs717620 genotype
  (Table 4 footnote); how this subject was coded is not stated.
* **Figure 8 cohort.** The covariate values used for the published single-dose
  and steady-state simulations are not reported (see the Figure 8 section).
* **Observed percentiles.** The VPC points are summaries of the S1 File
  computed by the maintainers, not values printed in the article. Values below
  the limit of detection are missing in that file and were excluded, which
  biases the observed EGC percentiles upward before the dose and at 9 h.
